ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$. A straight line passing through $O$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $G$ and $H$ (neither coinciding with the vertices of $\triangle ABC$) respectively. Let ${S}_{\mathrm{quadrilateral\ BCHG}}$ and ${S}_{\triangle AGH}$ represent the areas of the quadrilateral $BCHG$ and the triangle $AGH$, respectively. What is the maximum value of $\frac{{S}_{\mathrm{quadrilateral\ BCHG}}}{{S}_{\triangle AGH}}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Draw MN$\parallel$BC through O intersecting AB at N and AC at M. Draw ME$\parallel$AB through M intersecting GH at E. \\
Since O is the centroid of $\triangle ABC$, \\
therefore $\frac{AO}{OD}=2$, where D is the midpoint of BC \\
thus, BD=CD, $\frac{AO}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}$ \\
Since MN$\parallel$BC \\
therefore $\triangle AMN\sim \triangle ACB$ \\
therefore $\frac{NO}{BD}=\frac{MO}{CD}=\frac{AO}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AMN}}{{S}_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{AO}{AD}\right)^{2}=\frac{4}{9}$ \\
thus, MO=NO \\
Since ME$\parallel$AB \\
therefore $\angle MOH=\angle NOG$ \\
therefore $\triangle MOE\cong \triangle NOG$ (AAS) \\
therefore ${S}_{\triangle MOE}={S}_{\triangle NOG}$ \\
Let ${S}_{\triangle MEH}=x$, ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=9y$ \\
therefore ${S}_{\triangle AMN}=4y$, ${S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCMN}=5y$, \\
therefore ${S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCHG}={S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCMN}-{S}_{\triangle HOM}+{S}_{\triangle NOG}$ \\
$={S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCMN}-({S}_{\triangle MOE}+{S}_{\triangle MEH})+{S}_{\triangle NOG}$ \\
$=5y-x$ \\
${S}_{\triangle AHG}={S}_{\triangle AMN}-{S}_{\triangle NOG}+{S}_{\triangle HOM}$ \\
$={S}_{\triangle AMN}-{S}_{\triangle NOG}+({S}_{\triangle MOE}+{S}_{\triangle MEH})$ \\
$=4y+x$ \\
therefore $\frac{{S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCHG}}{{S}_{\triangle AGH}}=\frac{5y-x}{4y+x}$ \\
Since $x$ is a constant \\
therefore, as $y$ becomes smaller, the value of $\frac{{S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCHG}}{{S}_{\triangle AGH}}=\frac{5y-x}{4y+x}$ becomes larger \\
therefore, when $y=0$, $\frac{{S}_{\text{quadrangle}BCHG}}{{S}_{\triangle AGH}}=\boxed{\frac{5}{4}}$ is maximized, at this point GH$\parallel$BC

thus, BD=CD, $\frac{AO}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}$ \\

therefore $\triangle AMN\sim \triangle ACB$ \\
therefore $\frac{NO}{BD}=\frac{MO}{CD}=\frac{AO}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{{S}_{\triangle AMN}}{{S}_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{AO}{AD}\right)^{2}=\frac{4}{9}$ \\

Since ME$\parallel$AB \\
therefore $\angle MOH=\angle NOG$ \\
therefore $\triangle MOE\cong \triangle NOG$ (AAS) \\
therefore ${S}_{\triangle MOE}={S}_{\triangle NOG}$ \\
